lockedMove.speaker: William Lane Craig
lockedMove.proposition: Successive addition cannot convert a potential infinite into an actual infinite, even when every finite task is eventually performed, as illustrated by the Tristram Shandy story.
lockedMove.sourceExcerpt: can't convert a potential infinite into an actual infinite by successive addition or by Counting and that's why as I say set theory has been purged of all temporal notions you have to just have the actual infinite Gibbon tense lessly by the definition of set membership but you can't get there by successive addition and this is well illustrated in Russell's tristram shandy story

components.text: The decisive challenge is whether performing every finite task can instantiate an actual infinite without reaching an infinite ordinal.
The Tristram Shandy illustration is offered as a case-specific application of the claimed potential-to-actual prohibition.

response.rationale: The reply squarely reiterates that successive counting cannot convert potential infinity into actuality and offers a concrete story, but does not resolve the ordinal-cardinal distinction.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts both decisive demands and adds an example, while leaving their central conceptual objection unanswered.

precisionFindings.rationale: The potential-to-actual claim is clear, but formed, converted, and tenselessly given are not fully distinguished in scope.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The categorical prohibition is repeated despite the unresolved question whether a beginningless series is a conversion process.

charity.alternative: A beginningless series is not generated from an initial finite collection and therefore need not convert a potential infinite into an actual one.
charity.decisiveQualification: The argument must show that successive temporal ordering itself, without a first stage, constitutes the prohibited conversion.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The move risks assuming an initial finite state and therefore does not securely apply its conversion principle to a beginningless history.

immutableCompanionFields.words: Potential infinity consists only of indefinite finite growth and therefore cannot become an actual infinite merely through continued successive addition.

tags.label: Begging the question
tags.context: The move risks assuming that any infinite series must arise when a finite potential process crosses into actual completion.
